editorial:
The Lady Refuses is an RKO Radio Pictures drama released on March 8, 1931. George Archainbaud directed Betty Compson as June, a destitute young woman hired by a wealthy aristocrat, Sir Gerald Courtney, to pull his playboy son Russell, played by John Darrow, away from a gold digger. Gilbert Emery plays the father and Margaret Livingston plays the gold digger. Complications follow when June and the father fall for each other, and a murder adds to the trouble. It runs about 72 minutes. It suits anyone building a program of early-sound studio films, or looking for a Betty Compson vehicle.

The print status is still open. The 1958, 1959 and 1960 Catalog of Copyright Entries motion picture volumes yielded no renewal entry for the title in the searchable text reviewed, and the 28th-year window fell in 1959. Wikipedia also says the film went into the public domain in 1959 for lack of renewal. I did not find the original 1931 registration, and the catalog search was not exhaustive, so treat the print as probably free but unconfirmed. The score and the underlying story are also not confirmed as free here. Any modern transfer may add new titles, music or other material that carries its own rights. Check the specific copy you plan to use, not just the film.

Can I use the Internet Archive copy?

You can use the film itself, subject to the open status above. Treat any added music, titles or other material in that particular upload as separate and check it before reuse. A faithful scan adds no new copyright in the film.
